meaning: to cost much more money than you can afford
literal_translation: çok pahalıya mal olmak, bütçeyi zorlamak
example: A new phone can break the bank, so I will wait for a sale.
origin: Its exact origin is unclear; it is often linked to gambling games where a player could win all the money held by the bank.

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal misreading; the idiom is about the cost of something, not about crime

wrong_meanings.meaning: to open a new bank account
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Opening an account does not mean spending more money than you can afford
The idiom is about money, not about time or getting up

explanation: 'Break the bank' means that something costs far more money than you can afford. Use it when a price is too high for your budget.
